checks.detail: course.yaml and the brief both name Difference Equations and Stability as the formal prerequisite. The sequential prior lesson, Perching-Glider System Identification, is not a prerequisite but closes with an explicit forward handoff through a fitted conjugate root pair; this is valid narrative continuity and must not be restated as a dependency.

equations: exp(j(omega+2 pi k)n)=exp(j omega n) for integer n,k
checks.example: f=1000 Hz and f_s=8000 samples/s give omega=pi/4=0.7853981633974483 radians/sample.
checks.notation_guard: Use engineering j, dimensionless integer n, capital Omega only for dimensional angular frequency, and lowercase omega for discrete angular frequency.

checks.frequency_equivalence: Discrete complex exponentials are identical when frequencies differ by 2 pi k.
checks.time_periodicity: exp(j omega n) is periodic in n iff omega/(2 pi) is rational; its period is the least positive integer N satisfying omega N=2 pi m for some integer m.
checks.warning: Modulo-2pi frequency equivalence does not imply that every discrete sinusoid is periodic.

checks.conventions: peak amplitude A=2, initial phase phi=pi/4 modulo 2pi, omega=pi/3 radians/sample

checks.equation: A cos(omega n+phi)=(A/2)e^(j phi)e^(j omega n)+(A/2)e^(-j phi)e^(-j omega n)
checks.engineering_phasor_alternative: P=Ae^(j phi)=2e^(j pi/4), with x[n]=Re{P e^(j omega n)}
checks.guard: The engineering phasor P and the positive-frequency coefficient C_plus=P/2 are not the same amplitude convention.

checks.detail: Under exp(+j omega n), positive omega rotates counterclockwise and negative omega clockwise. Since exp(-j omega n)=conj(exp(j omega n)), a real sinusoid requires conjugate coefficients C_minus=conj(C_plus). For real discrete spectra, the negative-frequency value is the conjugate of its positive-frequency partner.
checks.self_conjugate_boundaries: omega=0 and omega=pi modulo 2pi are their own negative-frequency partners; the corresponding real-signal coefficients are real and arbitrary quadrature phase is not identifiable.

checks.convention: Take A>=0 and phase modulo 2pi; otherwise (-A,phi+pi) is an additional equivalent parameterization.
cases: At A=0, phase and frequency are unidentifiable.
At omega=0, x[n]=A cos(phi), so A and phi collapse to one constant unless extra constraints are imposed.
At omega=pi, x[n]=A cos(phi)(-1)^n, so the sine quadrature vanishes and A and phi again collapse.
phi and phi+2 pi k produce the same signal.
For a real cosine, (omega,phi) and (-omega,-phi) are equivalent in addition to omega modulo 2pi.

checks.result: verified under the course analysis-sign convention
checks.definition: For x[n]=a cos(omega n)+b sin(omega n), define P=a-jb so x[n]=Re{P e^(j omega n)}.
checks.recovery: A=hypot(a,b), phi=atan2(-b,a), with phase undefined when A=0.
checks.matched_integer_cycle_detector: I=(2/N)sum x[n]cos(omega n), Q=-(2/N)sum x[n]sin(omega n), P=I+jQ=Ae^(j phi), provided the sampled sine/cosine pair is orthogonal over the declared N-sample interval and omega is neither DC nor Nyquist.
checks.sign_alignment: The minus on the sine correlation matches the notation ledger's exp(-j omega n) analysis convention.

checks.definition: E=sum over the declared finite interval of x[n]^2; an eternal sinusoid is a power signal and does not have finite total energy.
checks.phase_independence_condition: The doubled-frequency sum sum exp(j2 omega n) over the interval must vanish. A whole number of periods supplies this for a nonzero, non-Nyquist discrete frequency.
checks.warmup_one_period: For A=2, omega=pi/3, and n=0..5, E=NA^2/2=12 for every phi.
checks.boundary: At omega=0 or pi, E=NA^2 cos^2(phi), so phase can change the interval energy; these are the self-conjugate exceptions.

checks.conditions: x[n]=A cos(omega n+phi), a declared N-sample orthogonal integer-cycle interval, A>0, and omega not congruent to 0 or pi
checks.single_cosine_projection: I=(2/N)sum x[n]cos(omega n)=A cos(phi), with nulls at phi=pi/2 and 3pi/2.
checks.quadrature_pair: Q=-(2/N)sum x[n]sin(omega n)=A sin(phi), so hypot(I,Q)=A and atan2(Q,I)=phi modulo 2pi.
checks.demo_consequence: In exact arithmetic and without noise, the I/Q pair has zero amplitude and phase error for every nonzero-amplitude phase; thresholds need a declared finite phase test set and numerical tolerance.

checks.coefficient_convention: Equivalently P=0.20 in Re{P z^n}; the two conjugate modal coefficients are 0.10 each.
checks.boundary: For forward n>=0, 0<=rho<1 decays, rho=1 is sustained, and rho>1 grows. The statement reverses backward in time; at rho=0 the angle is undefined and the nonzero mode dies after its initial sample.

checks.detail: The prior closing reports rho approximately 0.910206, omega approximately 0.29430 rad/sample, 0.04684 cycles/sample, and approximately 1.87 Hz at 40 samples/s. Recalculation from its displayed rounded root agrees. Its more precise root 0.8710731+j0.2640202 gives rho=0.9102060269805129 and omega=0.2942962366776272, explaining harmless last-digit differences.

checks.eternal_or_steady_state_input: For h[0]=h0, h[1]=h1, h[2]=h2 and x[n]=e^(j omega n) for all integer n, y[n]=e^(j omega n)(h0+h1e^(-j omega)+h2e^(-j2 omega)).
checks.connection: The parenthesized complex multiplier is H(e^(j omega)), the frequency response introduced in the next lesson.
checks.startup_boundary: If the intended input is u[n]e^(j omega n) from initial rest, y[0]=h0 and y[1]=e^(j omega)(h0+h1e^(-j omega)); the full eigenfunction factor applies only from n>=2 for this FIR.

issues.detail: The warm-up asks for 'the positive-frequency phasor' of a peak-amplitude real cosine without saying whether that means the engineering phasor P=Ae^(j phi) or the two-sided positive-frequency coefficient C_plus=(A/2)e^(j phi). For the stated tone these are 2e^(j pi/4) and e^(j pi/4), respectively. Name the convention and explicitly relate P=2C_plus.

The conjugate-pair/IQ recovery exercise and strategy-choice exercise do not define whether Q is a plus-sine coefficient, a negative-sine coefficient, or the imaginary part of an exp(-j omega n) correlation, and they omit normalization and interval conditions. To match the ledger, define I=(2/N)sum x cos and Q=-(2/N)sum x sin on a non-DC/non-Nyquist orthogonal integer-cycle interval, so P=I+jQ and phi=atan2(Q,I).

QuadratureDetectorLab gives error thresholds but no tone amplitude/frequency, sample count, endpoint convention, phase test grid or seed, estimator formulas, normalization, noise model, or zero-amplitude exclusion. 'For every phase' is not a finite automated test, and phase error is undefined at zero amplitude. Freeze a nonzero amplitude range, an orthogonal record, a deterministic phase set/seed, circular phase error, and exact pass aggregation.

The ledger says phase is modulo 2pi but does not select a display interval. Exact outputs at the negative real axis can be plus pi or minus pi depending on atan2 and signed zero. Declare a canonical interval such as (-pi,pi], compare phase with circular error, and never score phase when magnitude is zero.

The forward exercise says to pass e^(j omega n) through a three-tap FIR but does not state whether the exponential exists for all integer n or starts at n=0 from rest. The eigenfunction factorization is exact for the eternal/steady-state input; a causal startup has two partial-overlap outputs before the full H(e^(j omega)) multiplier applies. Declare the support or explicitly ask for both cases.

The brief routes Oppenheim-Schafer to Chapter 2 sections 2.1-2.2 and Chapter 5 for exponential sequences and LTI eigenfunctions. The direct locations are section 2.1.1 for complex sequences/periodicity, section 2.6.1 for LTI eigenfunctions, and section 2.8 for real-signal conjugate symmetry. Chapter 5 is downstream frequency-response/system-phase material, not the primary pointer for this lesson's basic claims.

The brief lists only Schaedler Lessons 7-8 and 16-17. Those support projections, radians, complex rotation, and Euler, but the intended frequency-equivalence, one-projection-null, conjugacy/DC/Nyquist, and equal-frequency-addition claims reside in Lessons 9-12, 19-21, 23, and 27. Add only the exact lesson pointers actually used.
